samples.summary: Canonical pagination doc still states the old `resolvePageSetup` contract while the change turns it into a validating/clamping read path
samples.evidence: docs-pagination.md:96-97 still says: "A helper `resolvePageSetup(setup: PageSetup | undefined): PageSetup` returns `setup ?? DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP`". The diff rewrites `resolvePageSetup` in packages/docs/src/model/types.ts into the single validating read path for every consumer (editor, ruler, MemDocStore, YorkieDocStore, CLI pagination, PDF export): it substitutes defaults for non-finite/negative/zero dimensions and proportionally shrinks margins via `fitMargins`/`MIN_CONTENT_PX`. The new "Page setup UI" section added to the same doc documents only the *write*-side `RangeError`, not the read-side clamp, so the doc now describes a contract the code no longer has — an architecture/data-model behaviour change without the design-doc update CONTRIBUTING requires.
searchedFor: read docs/design/docs/docs-pagination.md:80-120 and the new Page setup UI section in the diff

samples.summary: DOCX design doc's `<w:sectPr>` mapping not updated for the new import-time fallback/clamping behaviour
samples.evidence: docs-docx-import-export.md:315-321 still documents a straight twips→px mapping for `<w:pgSz>`/`<w:pgMar>`. The diff changes `parsePageSetup` to drop non-numeric/negative/zero page dimensions (falling back to the Letter default), to drop non-numeric/negative margins, and to route the whole result through `resolvePageSetup`, which can proportionally shrink author-specified margins. That is an observable import-fidelity change (a Word file whose margins exceed its page no longer round-trips its stated margins) with no record in the subsystem doc that owns the mapping.

samples.summary: Change reaches well past the task's stated "pure wiring" scope: serializer URL policy, model read-path clamping, DOCX import clamping and altered format-painter capture
samples.evidence: docs/tasks/active/20260829-docs-surface-existing-features-todo.md:3-5 defines the task as "pure wiring: no new document behaviour, no new file formats, no new model fields", and its acceptance list (line 57) includes "The keyboard shortcuts behave exactly as before". The diff nonetheless changes shipped engine behaviour on paths the wiring did not need: `serializeMarkdown` now drops hrefs/image sources (changing existing `wafflebase docs content --format md` output, e.g. any URL containing a space or a relative-with-authority target), `resolvePageSetup` clamps for every consumer, `parsePageSetup` rewrites imported geometry, and `captureFormatAtCursor` now reads the selection start and strips `href`/`image`/`pageNumber`, so `Mod+Shift+C`/`Mod+Alt+V` do not behave exactly as before. Most of it is defensible hardening and is recorded in the task's review follow-ups and in cli.md, but it is scope the issue explicitly excluded and it ships user-visible export/import changes under a wiring-only task.

samples.summary: The "margins must leave room for content" rule now exists in three independent implementations that can diverge
samples.evidence: The new design-doc text claims "the invariant is stated once on the write instead of once per UI that respects it" (docs/design/docs/docs-pagination.md, Page setup UI section), but the change actually adds a second and third statement of it: `assertUsablePageSetup` in packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts (throws on `left+right >= width`), `fitMargins`/`usableMargin` in packages/docs/src/model/types.ts (clamps with a 1 px floor), and the dialog's own `error` computation here (disables Apply on `parsed.left! + parsed.right! >= pageWidth`), alongside the ruler's 20 px rule. Three copies of one geometric rule with three different responses (throw / clamp / disable) is exactly the drift the repo's reuse discipline exists to avoid; the dialog copy in particular exists only for the message and could read the engine's predicate.

samples.summary: Export-time URL policy forked: the Markdown serializer's `isEmittableUrl` and the PDF exporter's bare `isSafeUrl` now give different answers for the same document
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/export/pdf-painter.ts:834 gates hyperlinks with plain `isSafeUrl` (imported from `../view/url-detect.js`), while the new `isEmittableUrl` in markdown.ts adds a whitespace/control-character gate, a relative-reference allowance and a scheme-relative rejection. Two exporters of the same document therefore disagree about which hrefs survive. docs/design/shared-core-extraction.md hoisted URL safety into `@wafflebase/core/url` precisely because "a rule enforced by two copies is a rule that drifts"; the new predicate is a generic emit-time URL rule that would fit there (or in a shared docs helper) rather than only in the Markdown serializer.

samples.summary: Toolbar painter is single-shot while the keyboard shortcut pair stays sticky, so the two surfaces disagree about the held buffer
samples.evidence: `FormatPainterToggle`'s second press calls `pasteFormat()` then `clearCopiedFormat()` (single-shot, Google-Docs-like), while the `Mod+Shift+C`/`Mod+Alt+V` path deliberately keeps the buffer for repeated pastes, and the slides `FormatPainterButton` (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/format-painter.tsx) is a pointer-driven paint mode. A format picked up with the keyboard and then pasted with the button is silently dropped afterwards. The task records this as a known limitation, so it is a taste/consistency point rather than a missed criterion.

samples.evidence: The review follow-up says "`NON_PAINTABLE_INLINE_KEYS` in `text-editor.ts` strips them", but the implementation in packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts strips `image`/`pageNumber`/`href` via a rest-destructuring in `captureFormatAtCursor`; a repo-wide grep for `NON_PAINTABLE_INLINE_KEYS` matches only this task file.
